title: Merrick Neck in Historical Records
summary: Merrack Neck appears in a 1658 record, preserving an early form of the Merrick name in the South Shore landscape.
address_label: Merrick Neck documentary reference; village location unconfirmed
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as a south shore community and bay landscape.
why_this_matters: Names such as Merrack Neck carry traces of an older coastal geography into the present. They connect familiar South Shore places with the Native history behind the Merrick name.
introduction_content:
William M. Beauchamp’s Aboriginal Place Names of New York records the name Merrack Neck in 1658. The spelling belongs to the many historical forms of Merrick found in Long Island records.

Along the South Shore, necks of land extend toward the bays between tidal creeks. These waterways shaped travel, fishing, and the names people used for the coast.
preservation_content: Historical shorelines, waterways, and property descriptions require comparison with dated maps before they can support a location. Evidence of a named neck should not be turned into directions to an assumed archaeological place.
whereintheworld_content: Explore the wider Merrick landscape and the nearby Milburn Creek history to learn more about the coast’s recorded names and community life.
